Question: Andy’s lawn has twice as much area as Beth’s lawn and three times as much area as Carlos’ lawn. Carlos’ lawn mower cuts half as fast as Beth’s mower and one third as fast as Andy’s mower. If they all start to mow their lawns at the same time, who will finish first?

Choices.D: Andy and Carlos tie for first.

Solution:
Finishing time depends on both the lawn area and the mowing rate:
\[
\text{time}=\frac{\text{area}}{\text{area cut per unit time}}.
\]
Only ratios are given, so choose common units in which Andy's, Beth's, and Carlos' lawn areas are \(12,6,4\), respectively. These satisfy both area comparisons. Their mowing rates can likewise be measured as \(3,2,1\), since Carlos cuts half as fast as Beth and one third as fast as Andy. Choosing common units rescales everyone's time by the same positive factor, so it preserves who finishes first.

Their completion times, in the same time unit, are
\[
t_A=\frac{12}{3}=4,\qquad
t_B=\frac{6}{2}=3,\qquad
t_C=\frac{4}{1}=4.
\]
Beth finishes first, choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
